feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. Evidence so far: iteration 0 (12 mm, 0.04 m spacing) had 2.15 oval line-loss events per run and max_error at the 0.06 m floor on every track. Iteration 1 (0.03 m spacing, weights rescaled to 25 per metre) removed oval line losses but cut progress on every track, which says spread is not the lever. Integration work for this geometry: the weights are 25 times sensor x, which is the same steering gain as the baseline, so no gain was changed. The only controller change is none; kp 3.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.2, base_speed 2.0 and last_direction recovery are kept from the baseline. If the next race shows oval line_loss_events falling with progress still near 0.19, the limit is steering lag, not footprint: keep this geometry and let the Integrator tune gains. If line losses stay high, the footprint was not the cause, and the next geometry test should be a forward sensor lead at y = 0.06 with the same spread.
requested_changes: If the next race shows oval line_loss_events falling below about 0.5 while progress stays under 0.25, keep sensor_size at 0.016 and the 0.16 m spread, and change only the sensor lead to y = 0.06 to give more steering lead. Evidence: the baseline max_error sat at the 0.06 m floor on all tracks, and the slalom lost progress early (0.03) with no line losses, which points to late steering.

If the next race shows max_error above 0.06 with line losses still near baseline, try sensor_size 0.016 with the outer sensors pulled in to x = -0.06 and 0.06 at y = 0.04, keeping weights at 25 per metre of x (-1.5, -0.75, 0, 0.75, 1.5). Evidence: iteration 1 showed the 0.03 m spacing kept the line in view but lost progress, so pull in only if the footprint change alone does not reduce max_error.

If steering_oscillation rises above the baseline 0.10 on the oval with completion intact, reduce wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10, or raise mass from 0.8 to 1.0, to lower turn authority or raise yaw inertia. Evidence: baseline oscillation was 0.10 on the oval and 0.08 on the s-bend.
